text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up re: assertion propagation across hosted -> dedicated -> private. We're seeing authz drift because different services attach different headers. How do we get to one canonical envelope?
Luis Ortega: Definitely needed. The two main pieces are tenant identity and caller intent. Also need a stable assertion id for tracing.
Maya Chen: Sketch: one header X-RW-Assertion with a tiny base64 JSON payload + sig metadata. e.g. 
```
X-RW-Assertion: v=1;alg=hs1;payload=eyJ0aWQiOiJ0ZXN0Iiwic2lkIjoiYXBpIiwgImFpZCI6IjEyMyJ9;sig=abcd...
```
Ivy Patel: Prefer short-lived tokens vs long-lived signatures to limit leakage surface. TTL 30s-2m seems reasonable.
Tom Novak: Private customers will want verification via local KMS. That means adapters at the private edge must be able to validate/translate assertions. We need a contract for that translation so semantics aren't lost.
Maya Chen: Right. Proposal: control-plane signs platform assertions. Private adapter can accept platform-signed assertion, validate via a mutually-agreed cert or handshake, then emit a local assertion signed by customer's KMS. Adapter MUST emit audit event mapping original aid -> new aid.
Luis Ortega: Questions: who rotates platform signing keys? how do hosted fallbacks validate when customer KMS is unavailable?
Ivy Patel: Platform keys rotated by control plane; verify path will accept either platform key or a delegated adapter signature. For fallback, runtime may accept platform-signed assertions if tenant config allows it. We should make this tenant-configurable.
Tom Novak: Important: translation MUST be monotonic in privileges. Adapter cannot add flags like "is_admin":true unless explicitly authorized. Let's create an assertion mapping table that lists allowed translations and forbidden mutations.
Maya Chen: Observability: include aid (assertion id) and truncated hash in traces/logs. No raw keys or payloads in logs. Also add a tracing baggage key so we can correlate when assertion is translated.
Luis Ortega: Fallback behavior options for a runtime that can't verify signature: 1) reject; 2) call translation endpoint on adapter; 3) accept if the signature is from the platform and tenant opted in. We should default to reject, and enable the other behaviors via tenant flags.
Ivy Patel: For performance, avoid blocking KMS calls inline. Verifier lib should support fast-hotswappable verification (HS vs PK modes). We can publish small reference shims for adapters: Go verifier, Node shim.
Tom Novak: Audit schema: {event_type, orig_aid, new_aid, adapter_id, timestamp, mapping_diff}. Also emit metrics for translation failures.
Maya Chen: Ops-bot, please add a checklist to hosting-handbook: canonical header spec, TTL guidance, adapter translation contract, tenant flag options, audit schema, verifier libraries.
ops-bot: Added TODO 9321 to hosting-handbook -> "Assertion envelope & adapter translation playbook". Assigned to @Maya Chen, @Tom Novak.
Luis Ortega: I'll start a spike for the Go verifier and RFC draft for header grammar.
Ivy Patel: I'll add negative test cases to eval suite: translation that tries to drop "sensitive" or escalate privileges must fail.
Tom Novak: Rollout approach? tenant-by-tenant opt-in seems safest. We should gate adapter translation behind a feature flag and opt-in per tenant in staging first.
Maya Chen: Agreed. Action items: Maya -> RFC + header grammar; Tom/Ivy -> adapter contract + audit; Luis -> verifier lib + reference shims. Target: staging canary in three weeks.
Luis Ortega: noted. I'll also document the failure modes to include in the RFC.
Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll post RFC link when it's ready. :thumbsup:
